title: Halftone Dot Screen Shader with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a halftone dot screen post-processing shader effect with a toggleable physics debug wireframe overlay.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Create a ground plane (20x20, gray #555555) at y=0.
- Place 5 colored spheres (radius 0.5) at y=3 with x positions [-4, -2, 0, 2, 4]. Colors: red, green, blue, yellow, cyan. Each sphere has a simple gravity simulation: velocity starts at 0, gravity = -9.81 m/s², bounce off ground with restitution coefficient 0.7. Track each sphere's velocity and position. Spheres should bounce continuously.
- Place a rotating torus knot (radius 2, tube 0.5, color #ff6600) at position (0, 4, -5) rotating on Y axis at 0.5 rad/s.

HALFTONE POST-PROCESSING:
- Implement a custom halftone dot screen shader as a post-processing pass using THREE.ShaderPass with EffectComposer (import from three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/).
- The halftone shader should convert the rendered scene into a pattern of circular dots whose size varies with luminance.
- Shader uniforms:
  - dotSize: float, default 4.0, range [1.0, 20.0] — controls the radius of halftone dots
  - resolution: vec2 — screen resolution
  - angle: float, default 0.0 radians — rotation angle of the dot grid pattern
  - scale: float, default 1.0, range [0.5, 5.0] — scale of the dot grid spacing
  - enabled: bool, default true — whether halftone effect is active
- The fragment shader should: compute screen-space grid cells, calculate distance from cell center, compare against luminance-derived threshold to produce dot pattern.

PHYSICS DEBUG OVERLAY:
- When toggled on, render wireframe bounding spheres around each physics sphere and velocity vectors as line segments (from sphere center, direction = velocity, length proportional to speed, max length 3 units).
- Debug overlay uses a separate THREE.Scene rendered on top (no clear) or add wireframe meshes to main scene.
- Debug overlay shows: wireframe spheres (white), velocity arrows (magenta lines).

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Key 'H': Toggle halftone shader on/off (sets the enabled uniform).
- Key 'D': Toggle physics debug overlay on/off.
- Key 'R': Reset all spheres to initial positions (y=3, velocity=0).
- Key 'ArrowUp': Increase dotSize by 1.0 (clamp to max 20.0).
- Key 'ArrowDown': Decrease dotSize by 1.0 (clamp to min 1.0).
- Key 'ArrowLeft': Decrease halftone angle by 0.1 radians.
- Key 'ArrowRight': Increase halftone angle by 0.1 radians.
- Key 'S': Increase scale by 0.5 (clamp to max 5.0).
- Key 'A': Decrease scale by 0.5 (clamp to min 0.5).
- Click on canvas: Apply an upward impulse of +5 m/s to all spheres' y-velocity.

HUD:
- Top-left overlay div showing:
  - 'Halftone: ON/OFF'
  - 'Dot Size: X.X'
  - 'Angle: X.XX rad'
  - 'Scale: X.XX'
  - 'Debug: ON/OFF'
  - 'Spheres Bouncing: N' (count of spheres currently with |velocityY| > 0.1)
- Style: white text, black semi-transparent background, monospace font, id='hud'.

STATE MANAGEMENT — window.__3D_STATE__:
Expose and continuously update:
- halftoneEnabled: boolean
- dotSize: number
- angle: number (radians)
- scale: number
- debugOverlayEnabled: boolean
- spherePositions: array of 5 {x, y, z} objects
- sphereVelocities: array of 5 {x, y, z} objects
- spheresBouncing: number (count with |vy| > 0.1)
- torusRotationY: number (current Y rotation in radians)
- frameCount: number (incremented each frame)
- totalKineticEnergy: number (sum of 0.5 * mass * vy^2 for all spheres, mass=1)
- lastImpulseFrame: number (frame when last click impulse was applied, default -1)
- resetCount: number (how many times R was pressed, starts 0)

ENSURE:
- Physics runs with fixed dt = 1/60.
- All state values are NaN-free at all times.
- The halftone shader compiles and renders without errors.
- EffectComposer renders the final output.
- Animation loop uses requestAnimationFrame.
physics_constraints: Gravity = -9.81 m/s², restitution = 0.7 on ground bounce (vy *= -0.7 when y <= 0.5), spheres must not fall below y=0.5 (radius 0.5 on ground at y=0). Kinetic energy must decrease or stay equal after each bounce (energy loss from restitution). All positions and velocities must be NaN-free.
